body.p: provides an intuitive browser-based user interface designed for productivity and efficient collaboration.
Most screens follow this general layout pattern:

section.title: Top header stripe
section.p: This contains shortcuts to the application home screen, to the list of projects and review tasks, access to user profile and the help menu. In addition, it shows information about the current resource you are working with, such as the project or the review task.

section.title: Left vertical stripe
section.p: This contains in the top part the list of possible views for the current working area, while in the bottom part there are shortcuts to open other working areas.

section.title: Current view
section.p: This contains content of the current view selected in the .

section.title: Main working area
section.p: This usually contains the visual editor with its helper side views.

fig.title: The general UI pattern when accessing a project

body.p: In this example, the shows the home button, the current project name, and the current branch in the top-left area. It also shows shortcuts to the projects and review task lists, and the user and help menu buttons in the top-right area. It also shows the current working area inside the project — in this case, Personal workspace — and other information related to the current task.

The shows the list of available views in the top part, with Files highlighted as the current view. The bottom part has shortcuts to other working areas of the project, including review tasks, the repository, defined deliverables, and project settings.
The shows the content of the current Files view.
The contains the visual editor and its helper side-views.
